conditions: synthetic Spanish/English words, documents with about 2.5 KB of content (title, tags, content) and memory items with about 1.2 KB; isolated PostgreSQL 17.11 in the kairos-test container (no CPU limit, nothing else running); maintenance_work_mem 256MB, serial index build; schema version 8 as starting point; measured with the FINAL schema (indexes without predicate)
reading: Store.migrate() runs the whole schema in ONE transaction, so the strongest lock taken on each table is held until the COMMIT of the entire migration (first_migrate_seconds), not for the phase that took it. ALTER TABLE takes ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on BOTH documents (generated columns: full rewrite, the dominant cost) and memory_items (ADD COLUMN is metadata only, but its lock is kept): reads and writes of both tables by the services of the previous release wait for the whole run. The phase times are per statement on a copy and only show where the time goes (they do not sum to the total: the total also contains the earlier idempotent versions and the migration's own overhead). A repeated migrate skips the whole block (no lock, no scan).
disk: total relation size (table + indexes + TOAST) grows 2.5x for documents (37 -> 92 MB) and 3x for memory_items (30 -> 91 MB) at 20,000 rows; the documents rewrite needs room for a second copy of the table during the run and the transaction writes WAL for every changed row
deployed_volume_note: the deployed database holds about 21 documents (activation of 2026-11-09): the migration is sub-second there; the figures above only bound the cost for a much larger installation
earlier_measurement: the first version of this file (119.3 s at 20,000 rows) was taken with the six indexes still partial and other containers running; superseded by this one
what: wall time of Store.migrate() over an existing schema-8 database; phases timed per statement on a second copy
